newsitem.title: USA: Int'l Network shares released from lock-up.
newsitem.headline: Int'l Network shares released from lock-up.

text.p: International Network Services said Morgan Stanley & Co Inc agreed to release up to one million shares from "lock-up" agreements executed prior to the company's initial public offering.
The shares affected by the agreement were held by current employees, other than executives, and former employees, the company said.

Under "lock-up" agreements, company employers or insiders are often prevented from selling shares immediately after an initial public offering. Once the shares are released from "lock-up" pact, insiders can hold or sell the shares as they choose.
Morgan Stanley acted a as representative of the underwriting group of the company's September initial public offering.
International Network Services, which provides services for complex enterprise networks, launched its initial public offering in September.
